title: Tenant isolation and multi-region failover: circuit breakers, load-shedding, and safe upgrades for Dedicated/Private control planes
creator: Ava Chen
description: Deliver a cross-team reliability effort to ensure Dedicated and Private control planes tolerate region failures, noisy-tenants, and rolling upgrades without violating customer SLOs. Workstreams: 1) Define per-tenant SLOs and failure isolation boundaries; 2) Implement per-tenant and per-pool circuit breakers that trip on sustained resource pressure or error spikes; 3) Add load-shedding policies (reserved vs best-effort vs burst) and an admission controller for burst throttling; 4) Design multi-region failover with health checks, topology-aware routing, and state reconciliation; 5) Upgrade safety: canary control plane upgrades, automatic rollback triggers, and tenant-level upgrade fencing for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: SLOs defined and documented: availability SLOs per-tenant (regional and global) and P99/P95 latency buckets for control plane operations
Circuit breakers implemented and configurable per-tenant/pool with documented thresholds and cooldown behavior
Load-shedding policy enforces reserved capacity, sheds best-effort traffic under sustained pressure, and preserves SLA-backed reservations
Automated multi-region failover demo: simulated region outage results in <60s traffic redirection for critical control-plane calls and no cross-tenant impact beyond shed traffic
Upgrade canary runs and automated rollback succeed in a staged rollout without cascading tenant failures
Observability: metrics, traces, and alerts for breaker state, shed-rate, failover events, and upgrade rollbacks are available in Console dashboards
Runbook and incident playbook written and reviewed by SRE and Solutions teams
implementation_notes: Design decision: prioritize per-tenant resource limits and soft quotas over global throttles to reduce blast radius
Circuit breaker semantics follow a token + error-rate hybrid: short-term token exhaustion triggers immediate fast-fail; sustained error-rate crosses open the breaker for a cooldown window
Use existing routing layer to support active-active multi-region for Dedicated customers with region preference and active-passive for Private if required by networking policies
Load-shedding implementation will extend admission controller to tag requests by QoS: reserved, baseline, burst. Baseline uses adaptive token-bucket tied to current pool capacity metrics
Upgrade safety: implement 'tenant-fence' flag to pin control-plane operations off a node pool during upgrades, combined with health-check based canary groups
Telemetry: emit breaker_state, shed_rate_by_tenant, failover_count, upgrade_rollback_count, and tenant_latency_histograms to enable SLO dashboards
tasks: TC1: Draft SLO matrix and run it by Product and Solutions for Dedicated and Private customers
TC2: Implement per-tenant circuit breaker library in runtime agent and add config endpoints in control plane
TC3: Extend admission controller with QoS tagging and rate limiter backed by pool capacity signals
TC4: Build failover orchestrator prototype that triggers route swaps and KV reconciliation during simulated region loss
TC5: Add canary rollout paths and automated rollback triggers for control plane service
TC6: Create Console dashboards and alerts; onboard SRE on runbook
TC7: Chaos tests and a cross-team tabletop exercise with Solutions and Support
risks: Mis-tuned breakers may cause over-shedding and surface false availability incidents
State reconciliation after failover may lead to transient duplicate jobs unless idempotency guarantees are enforced
Private deployments with strict networking may limit automated failover capabilities, requiring manual runbook steps
Upgrade fencing adds complexity; incorrect fencing could leave tenants pinned to unhealthy control-plane replicas
tradeoffs: Per-tenant strict isolation increases operational complexity and code paths but substantially lowers blast radius
Active-active multi-region reduces failover time at cost of more complex state sync; active-passive is simpler but increases RTO
Conservative shedding preserves reserved customers at the expense of best-effort throughput under peak load
